scenes.meaning: Heat is becoming a persistent condition rather than only an exceptional day.
scenes.causal_boundary: Describe measured warming/heat exposure; do not attribute every hot day or event solely to climate change.

scenes.meaning: Dense urban form and humidity can turn temperature into a larger human heat burden.
scenes.causal_boundary: Keep city-scale heat-island and heat-index claims at the resolution supported by the source.

scenes.meaning: Heat enters the working day through physical strain, hydration needs, breaks and reduced capacity.
scenes.causal_boundary: Use aggregate/documented worker experiences; do not assign symptoms to an invented real worker as fact.

scenes.meaning: Factories are not insulated from the climate outside; indoor heat can persist across a long season.
scenes.causal_boundary: Evidence comes from sampled factories; do not universalize exact temperatures or conditions to every Bangladesh factory.

scenes.meaning: For informal outdoor workers, avoiding heat can mean giving up paid hours.
scenes.causal_boundary: Income/time-loss figures belong to the surveyed population and period.

scenes.meaning: Lost workdays turn heat exposure into household income pressure.
scenes.causal_boundary: Do not extrapolate surveyed percentage losses to all Dhaka households.

scenes.meaning: At national scale, accumulated lost work becomes a macroeconomic constraint.
scenes.causal_boundary: National workday-loss estimates are modeled/estimated and must be labelled accordingly.

scenes.meaning: The end of a shift does not necessarily end heat exposure; homes can remain part of the heat system.
scenes.causal_boundary: Use studied worker homes/household survey conditions; do not invent a named household or exact dwelling.

scenes.meaning: Recovery depends on housing, cooling access, time and household resources.
scenes.causal_boundary: Evidence supports unequal capacity to cope, not a universal household experience.
scenes.knowledge_stop: Exact household coping strategies and expenditure require locality/household evidence before factual narration.

scenes.meaning: Heat reaches children through health risk and disruption to schooling.
scenes.causal_boundary: Extreme-weather disruption has multiple causes; distinguish heatwave closures from other climate hazards.

scenes.meaning: School interruption shifts part of the burden back into households and children's time.
scenes.causal_boundary: Do not quantify household childcare, learning loss or income effects without specific evidence.
scenes.knowledge_stop: Household-level consequences of individual closures remain unresolved in this evidence pack.

scenes.meaning: Heat adaptation can be physical and operational: shade, airflow, cooling, hydration and work practices.
scenes.causal_boundary: Separate tested/measured interventions from recommendations or proposals.

scenes.meaning: Some factory cooling investments can repay through reduced heat-related losses.
scenes.causal_boundary: Payback estimates are study-specific economic estimates, not guaranteed returns.

scenes.meaning: Adaptation is also a distribution question: who can afford protection and who bears the residual heat.
scenes.causal_boundary: Frame as evidenced inequality/exposure and policy question; do not assign motives or predict policy outcomes.
scenes.knowledge_stop: Future allocation of adaptation costs and benefits is unresolved.
